questions.question: An app stores logged-in sessions in a JavaScript Map. After switching to cluster mode with 4 workers, users are randomly logged out. Why?
options: Each worker is a separate process with its own memory, so a session saved in one worker is missing in the others
Maps are not supported in cluster workers
The primary process deletes sessions on every fork
questions.explanation: Cluster workers do not share memory. Shared state such as sessions must move to an external store like Redis (or be carried in a stateless token) so any process can serve any request.

questions.question: Which is the recommended way to decide how many cluster workers to fork?
questions.explanation: os.availableParallelism() reports how many parallel tasks the machine can run and is the recommended replacement for os.cpus().length when sizing process or thread pools.

questions.question: You deploy a Node API on Kubernetes. What is the usual recommendation?
options: Run one Node process per container and scale with replicas
Run PM2 in cluster mode with max instances inside every container
Run all services in a single container to save memory
Disable SIGTERM handling so pods stop faster
questions.explanation: The orchestrator already restarts crashed containers and balances load across replicas, so one process per container keeps things simple. Each process should still handle SIGTERM for graceful shutdown.

questions.question: What does `pm2 reload api` provide that `pm2 restart api` does not?
options: It clears the PM2 log files
It converts fork mode to cluster mode
A rolling restart of cluster instances, so the app keeps serving requests during the restart
questions.explanation: In cluster mode, reload restarts instances one at a time, keeping others online, which gives a zero-downtime restart. restart stops and starts all instances together.
